trust_decision.summary: Do not let the telemetry tracker exist at all unless a builder supplies a token: the shipped build-time token 'secret' becomes an empty default, NewTracker returns a disabled Tracker before any fingerprint or client is built, and the runner only announces, starts and registers the tracker when Enabled() is true.

landing_point.why: The advisory names a hardcoded authentication token first, and this is the only hardcoded credential in the telemetry package; its value is what gets put in the Authorization header (telemetry/telemetry.go:145-147).

fix_sites.entry_point: telemetry.NewConfig() called from cli.WithTelemetry (cli/runner_options.go:190) at every server start
telemetry.NewConfig() (public API); Config.Token consumed by telemetry.NewTracker
exported Tracker type plus the new Enabled() method (public Go API)
anycable-go CLI (cmd/anycable-go/main.go:46) and embedded server (cli/embed.go:76 -> runNode)
Metrics.Run via cli/cli.go:284 (unrelated to the security property)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report names the telemetry subsystem, so the server runner's start-up call is a different subsystem (and with the token default gone the tracker is inert anyway); while for builds that do carry a vendor token the transmitted value is a SHA-256 fingerprint, an intentional opt-in rather than the shipped default.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Telemetry must keep working for builds that supply a token: TestTracking expects a boot event and a usage event with custom props (telemetry/telemetry_test.go:63-92), so an over-broad fix that deletes Collect/Send or strips properties breaks it; and a token-less Tracker must stay safe when a caller still uses it, because Shutdown closes a nil client (telemetry/telemetry.go:114) and Collect/Send dereference a nil logger/config (telemetry/telemetry.go:120, telemetry/telemetry.go:243) - so disabling NewTracker without also gating cli/cli.go:321-324 crashes the default binary at start-up or shutdown.

O6_input_shapes: no build-time token (empty after the fix) -> tracker disabled
non-empty token injected with -ldflags -X ...telemetry.auth=... in the release workflows -> tracker enabled
empty vs non-empty token is the only discriminator the fix adds; a nil *telemetry.Config is still dereferenced (telemetry/telemetry.go:63) and Endpoint/Debug/CustomProps are unchanged
ANYCABLE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true still disables telemetry one layer up at cli/runner_options.go:189
payload input shapes - argv slice, ANYCABLE_* env list, whole TOML config file - are not filtered by the fix at all

O8_uncovered_routes.route: boot and usage events transmit a digest of all process argv, including --secret/--jwt_secret/--api_secret flags
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only builds carrying a vendor token reach it, and the value is hashed, not the arguments themselves
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (telemetry), about 320 lines below the fix's constructor guard; producer untouched by the fix

O8_uncovered_routes.route: boot and usage events transmit a digest of every ANYCABLE_* environment variable pair
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Documented as anonymised telemetry; env values are hashed with the rest of the fingerprint
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (telemetry), same file as the fix, untouched

O8_uncovered_routes.route: boot and usage events transmit a digest of the entire TOML config file, which normally contains secret = "..." (config/config.go:36)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only applies when a config file is used, and a hash is not cleartext
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (telemetry), same file as the fix, untouched

O8_uncovered_routes.route: appProperties sends the raw ANYCABLEPLUS_APP_NAME environment value in cleartext as 'plus-name'
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A product/app name is not a secret; neighbouring AnyCable+ feature property
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 175 lines below the constructor guard

O8_uncovered_routes.route: appProperties tells the endpoint whether a shared secret is configured at all ('has-secret')
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A single boolean, part of the feature inventory the docs say is collected

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ANYCABLE_TELEMETRY_URL accepts any endpoint including plain http://, so the fingerprint and properties travel in cleartext when an operator sets an http URL
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The operator explicitly configured that endpoint; supported override knob
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different package (cli), adjacent to the fix's caller gate

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another environment-variable collector folded into the transmitted digest
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The collector already exists and generateDigest accepts any number of parts, so a maintainer adding one more deployment-identifying input would extend this list rather than add a new exporter.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another config- or env-derived property sent in cleartext beside plus-name and has-secret
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: appProperties is the single property-building function; adding a region/plan/distro value read straight from the environment is the obvious next change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an ANYCABLE_TELEMETRY_TOKEN env opt-in next to the existing ANYCABLE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY / ANYCABLE_TELEMETRY_URL knobs
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The option already reads two ANYCABLE_TELEMETRY_* variables, so letting self-builders enable telemetry with the same secret name CI uses is a natural addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second token source (runtime env var or file) beside the build-time variable
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Config is the only place telemetry settings are defaulted, and the CI secret is already called ANYCABLE_TELEMETRY_TOKEN, so reading it at runtime is a plausible alternative.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: config-derived default tags shipped to a third-party StatsD endpoint
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A second outbound exporter with DefaultTags already exists, so repeating the same deployment-identifier leak in the metrics subsystem costs a maintainer one line.

O9_family: CWE-798 hardcoded credential combined with CWE-312 exposure of sensitive configuration through a telemetry client

O10_build.toolchain: go.mod requires go 1.26.0 with toolchain go1.26.4; modules only (no vendor dir in-tree; CI runs 'go mod vendor')
services: redis (full test suite only; the telemetry package tests need none)
O10_build.project_tests: telemetry/telemetry_test.go::TestTracking drives NewTracker/Collect/collectUsage/Shutdown against an httptest server (fully offline); the whole suite is 'make test' -> go test -race ./... (Makefile:170-171), where Redis-backed packages need REDIS_URL.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Make the telemetry token configurable from an environment variable (or just delete anycableCLIArgs/anycableFileConfig from clusterFingerprint) and leave telemetry enabled by default, so argv/env/config-file data is still digested and sent whenever a token exists.

out_of_scope_notes: The fix commit also rewrites metrics/metrics.go (adds 'defer close(serverErr)', deletes the goroutine comment), which has nothing to do with the advisory and risks a send-on-closed-channel panic if the metrics server reports an error after Run returns - not pursued.
cli/options.go:445-446 prints the full configuration, including 'secret = ...' in cleartext (config/config.go:158-159), to stdout under --print-config; a different sink from telemetry - not pursued.
unverified: go build / go test were not run (no shell in this session); buildability is inferred from go.mod (go 1.26.0, go.sum present, no vendor dir, CI runs 'go mod vendor').
Repository size was not measured, so repo_mb is null and the tiny_repo red flag could not be confirmed or excluded (~260 Go files suggests a small-to-medium repo).

O12 regression_tests_in_pinned_commit rationale: telemetry/telemetry_test.go::TestTracking is already present at the pinned commit and is the only test the fix edits (it just adds tconf.Token = "secret"); the fix adds no new test, so hidden tests for the disabled path are not visible in the pinned tree.
O12 protection_documented_without_exceptions rationale: docs/telemetry.md:23 states an absolute no-collection list (including environment variables) with no exceptions.

O7 nuance: NewTracker is called unconditionally at cli/cli.go:319 and computes clusterFingerprint (thus reading os.Args, os.Environ and the config file) before the new Enabled() check at cli/cli.go:320; the check never inspects the produced digest, so no route filters the producer.

The O8 routes are payload producers feeding the single Send path (telemetry/telemetry.go:119-172); there is no second telemetry implementation or transport in the tree, so pattern-B strength is moderate rather than a separate endpoint.
Latest code for O8 was not available ('none'), so present_in_latest is unknown for every route.
